root.name: Ruy Lopez: Closed Berlin Defense, Chigorin Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 Nf6 4. O-O d6 5. d4 Nd7

overview: Black meets 5.d4 with 5...Nd7, keeping the e5 pawn and avoiding the Berlin endgame. White usually exchanges 6.Bxc6 bxc6 and builds with Nc3 and Re1, while Black has doubled c-pawns, the bishop pair chances and a very compact position. Play is slow and manoeuvring, with Black hard to break down.

white_ideas.idea: Exchange on c6 to ruin Black's pawns, then Nc3 and Re1 to pressure e5
Open the centre with dxe5 at the right moment

black_ideas.idea: Use the doubled c-pawns for central control and ...Nb6/...Nf6 regrouping

typical_structures.structure: Black doubled c-pawns against White's healthy queenside majority
Tension on e5/d4 that White can resolve with dxe5

character.notes: Black's position is compact and hard to crack; no forcing tactics early.

structure.notes: The e5/d4 tension stays unresolved for some time.

level.notes: Slow plans around e5 and the c-pawns need judgement more than memory.
